A legal roll from cell p = (pr,pc) to cell q = (qr,qc) with cost k is defined to hold if there exists a direction d = (dr,dc) in {(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)} and an integer k >= 1 such that q = (pr + k*dr, pc + k*dc), every cell (pr + i*dr, pc + i*dc) for 0 <= i <= k is empty, and the cell (pr + (k+1)*dr, pc + (k+1)*dc) is non-empty. A path from start to destination is a sequence of cells p0, p1, ..., pt with t >= 1, p0 = (start[0], start[1]), pt = (destination[0], destination[1]), such that for each 0 <= i < t there exists an integer k_i >= 1 with a legal roll from p_i to p_{i+1} of cost k_i; the total cost of the path is the sum of k_i for 0 <= i < t. Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds: if there exists at least one path from start to destination (as defined above), then r is the minimum total cost over all such paths; if no such path exists, then r = -1.
